output.summary: KEP-1771 proposes that external cloud providers standardize semantic versioning so that major and minor versions of their releases (e.g., cloud-controller-manager v1.18.X) track the Kubernetes version they support; patch versions need not match. Status is implementable, stage alpha.
output.rationale: External cloud providers had no standard for versioning their releases, and no documented version skew policy between cloud-controller-manager and Kubernetes, beyond an assumption based on the vendored k8s.io/kubernetes version. The KEP aims to make supported Kubernetes versions discoverable and reduce incompatibility from wide skew, such as an old vendored Kubernetes running on a much newer cluster. The readme also notes that users already upgrade cloud-controller-manager alongside Kubernetes, which supports tying the versions together.

alternatives.option: Don't standardize semantic versioning of releases for external cloud providers
alternatives.why_not: The readme lists this as the only alternative, and the KEP's goals of standardizing versioning and reducing skew-related incompatibilities are presented as the reason it was not chosen. The source gives no further rejection reasoning.

evidence.quote: This KEP proposes to standardize all external cloud providers on a semantic versioning policy that ensures the vendored version of the cloud-controller-manager library is likely to match the version of the Kubernetes control plane.
release v1.18.X of cloud-controller-manager for provider Foo should support Kubernetes clusters on v1.18.X.
In practice we've learned that users upgrade the cloud-controller-manager along upgrades to the Kubernetes version.
